title: Departure introductions

rows.text: Departure introductions
18 draft packages. Images have no embedded text; wording listed as an overlay is rendered separately.
OPEN-JOURNALIST-A · Seattle: File Under Unavailable

Treasury suspended Direct File for the 2026 tax season. You’re a Seattle reporter taking five companions to D.C. You have questions about why a service called Direct has developed such an elaborate detour.
Head for D.C. → You set out. The notebook accepts your questions without asking which premium package you need.
Scene: Seattle reporter holds an open blank notebook beside a laptop showing only a blank dark screen; five companions gather at the stationary van.
Source: GAO B-337954: Suspension of IRS Direct File (2026-05-12)
OPEN-JOURNALIST-B · Seattle: The Small Print in Space

Trump’s 2027 budget request seeks a 47 percent cut to NASA science. You’re a Seattle reporter taking five companions to D.C. Washington wants a smaller view of the universe. Your van has already achieved that with one cracked sun visor.
Start the journey → You head east. The visor stays down; the questions do not.

Scene: Seattle reporter and five companions gather beside the parked van; the bent sun visor and a rolled unlettered star chart are visible through the open door, with no vehicle damage beyond the cosmetic visor.
Source: American Astronomical Society: Policy Update, 8 April 2026 (2026-04-08)
Source: Lowell Observatory: This Week in Astronomy History, February 15–21 (undated)
OPEN-JOURNALIST-C · Seattle: Original Payment Method

DOT says qualifying cancelled flights require automatic refunds when passengers reject alternatives. You’re a Seattle reporter taking five companions to D.C. Your transport is a van. If this trip disappoints, the original payment method is everyone looking at everyone else.
Get on the road → You set out. Nobody accepts an apology redeemable only on another cross-country trip.
Scene: Seattle reporter gestures between the parked van and a blank airline leaflet; five companions stand with their modest bags, considering the trip rather than already traveling.
Source: DOT: What passengers need to know about the automatic refund rule (2024-11-18)
OPEN-LOBBYIST-A · Los Angeles: Difficult to Cancel

A court struck down the FTC’s click-to-cancel rule over its procedure. You’re a Los Angeles lobbyist taking five companions to D.C. You know how rules disappear. You’d like Washington to demonstrate the trick on your oldest subscription.
Head for D.C. → You leave. Cancelling the government’s interest in cancellation has been remarkably quick.
Scene: Los Angeles lobbyist holds a phone beside a long blank subscription bill curling toward the parked van; five companions wait with luggage, with no visible screen text.
Source: AP: Appeals court vacates FTC click-to-cancel rule (2025-07-09)
OPEN-LOBBYIST-B · Los Angeles: Claimed Property

Ohio allocated $600 million from unclaimed funds toward a Browns stadium. You’re a Los Angeles lobbyist taking five companions to D.C. Your gas money is very much claimed. Everybody is standing beside the van claiming there should be more.
Begin the trip → You set out. The glove box has declined to finance a stadium.
Scene: Los Angeles departure: lobbyist and five companions face a nearly empty cash tin on the van seat; a plain miniature football lies beside the lobbyist's blank Ohio news clipping.
Source: AP: Ohio budget allocates unclaimed funds toward Browns stadium (2025-07-01)
OPEN-LOBBYIST-C · Los Angeles: Total Price of Admission

The FTC now requires mandatory hotel and ticket fees in the upfront total. You’re a Los Angeles lobbyist taking five companions to D.C. The trip budget is finally transparent: you can see straight through it.
Set off east → You leave. Knowing the full price has removed the surprise without removing the price.
Scene: Los Angeles lobbyist holds a thin translucent budget envelope up to daylight; five companions wait beside their bags and the parked van; a blank lodging leaflet provides the context.
Source: FTC: Rule on Unfair or Deceptive Fees FAQ (Effective 2025-05-12)
OPEN-ORGANIZER-A · Portland: Compatible Humans
Oregon’s repair law limits software locks on replacement parts. You’re a Portland organizer taking five companions and your case to D.C. Everyone fits the van. Nobody requires manufacturer approval.
Leave for D.C. → You set out. The passengers install themselves without buying a seating license.
Scene: In Portland, the organizer holds a phone with a detached plain back cover while five named companions stand with their luggage beside the open, parked van; nobody has departed.
Source: Oregon Revised Statutes: Right to Repair Consumer Equipment (2025 codification)
OPEN-ORGANIZER-B · Portland: Mint Condition

Washington stopped making pennies that cost more than pennies. You’re a Portland organizer taking five companions to D.C. Your gas jar contains the old ones. For once, the government has spent more on your savings than you have.
Start the trip → You set out. The pennies remain legal tender, which is more than can be said for your optimistic fuel estimate.
Scene: Portland departure: the organizer tilts a modest coin jar while the five named companions inspect luggage beside the stationary van; scattered copper-colored coins carry no readable markings.
Source: United States Mint: Penny information (Current guidance checked 2026-09-14)
OPEN-ORGANIZER-C · Portland: Special Delivery

USPS changed delivery standards: some mail faster, some slower. You’re a Portland organizer taking five companions and your case to D.C. The government’s reply may take a scenic route. You’ve decided to arrive with the question.
Begin the journey → You leave Portland. Six people are harder to misplace behind a sorting machine.
Scene: Portland organizer beside five companions and a parked van; an oversized ordinary case folder rests against a small blank envelope, neither sent nor loaded yet.
Source: USPS announces refined service standards and cost reductions (2025-02-26)
OPEN-SATIRIST-A · San Diego: Roadworthy Monarchy

Trump celebrated his attempted congestion-toll reversal with “LONG LIVE THE KING!” The toll survived that celebration. You’re a San Diego satirist taking five companions to D.C. Your van offers monarchy’s traditional problem: everybody wants the front seat.
Start the trip → You pull away. The succession is settled by whoever remembered to fill the tank.
Scene: San Diego satirist and five companions gather by the parked van; a cheap paper crown without markings rests on the empty front passenger seat, nobody crowned or already aboard.
Source: New York governor’s transcript on the federal congestion-pricing reversal attempt (2025-02-19)
Source: Southern District of New York: Congestion-pricing opinion (2026-03-03)
OPEN-SATIRIST-B · San Diego: The Sugar Summit

Trump claimed credit for Coca-Cola’s additional cane-sugar drink. The old lineup stayed. You’re a San Diego satirist taking five companions to D.C. The country has two versions of a soft drink and you still have one version of broke.
Leave for D.C. → You set out. The cooler provides bipartisan support to whichever drinks were cheapest.
Scene: San Diego satirist holds two plain drink bottles beside a modest cooler; five companions stand with their bags near the parked van; no brand lettering or logos.
Source: Coca-Cola reports second-quarter 2025 results (2025-07-22)
Source: AP: Coca-Cola confirms a cane-sugar option after Trump’s claim (2025-07-22)
OPEN-SATIRIST-C · San Diego: Shoes of State

TSA generally lets passengers keep their shoes on now. You’re a San Diego satirist taking five companions to D.C. by van. After a look at the footwear, the crew requests that Washington consider jurisdiction over socks.
Get on the road → You leave. The shoes stay on; a window becomes foreign policy.
Scene: San Diego satirist and five companions stand beside the parked van; one scuffed pair of shoes sits next to an open gym bag, with no passenger removed or added.
Source: AP: TSA ends routine shoes-off airport screening (2025-07-08)
OPEN-STAFFER-A · Sacramento: Serious Serifs

Rubio sent State Department correspondence back to Times New Roman. You’re a Sacramento staffer taking five companions to D.C. Your case is already in the correct font. The people described in it remain inconveniently broke.
Leave for D.C. → You set out. Italics made the complaints lean forward, but someone still has to drive.
Scene: Sacramento staffer examines a blank printed page beside a closed laptop while five companions wait with bags at the parked van; all apparent typography must be an optional overlay.
Source: AP: Rubio orders return to Times New Roman (2025-12-10)
OPEN-STAFFER-B · Sacramento: Direct Deposit, Indirect Help

Trump began moving federal refund checks to electronic payments, with exceptions. You’re a Sacramento staffer taking five companions and your case to D.C. Washington can now move money without an envelope. Getting an answer still seems to require a van.
Start toward D.C. → You get underway. There is no box to tick for direct deposit of attention.
Scene: Sacramento departure: staffer compares a blank envelope and a dark phone screen; five companions and luggage wait beside the van with its engine off.
Source: IRS: Modernizing payments to and from America’s bank account (Current guidance checked 2026-09-14)
OPEN-STAFFER-C · Sacramento: Whole Government
Congress found time to put whole milk back on school-lunch menus. You’re a Sacramento staffer taking five companions and your rent petition to D.C. You consider submitting it in a milk carton.
Get underway → You leave Sacramento. The petition now has a handle and a better chance of reaching the lunch committee.
Scene: Sacramento staffer considers a blank rent-petition folder beside an empty plain milk carton with a carry handle; five companions wait at the parked van. The papers are not yet inserted.
Source: Public Law 119-69: Whole Milk for Healthy Kids Act of 2025 (2026-01-14)
OPEN-WHISTLEBLOWER-A · San Francisco: Hours Actually Worked

A DOE audit described a nuclear contractor billing for hours nobody worked. You’re a San Francisco whistleblower taking five companions and your case to D.C. The drive will take actual hours. It’s an embarrassing habit of yours.
Drive toward D.C. → You set out. The odometer refuses to accept estimated effort.
Scene: San Francisco whistleblower holds a blank audit folder beside the van's unnumbered instrument panel; five companions wait at the open doors before departure.
Source: Audit: DOE-OIG-25-36 (2025-11-26)
OPEN-WHISTLEBLOWER-B · San Francisco: Ten Out, One In

Trump told agencies to identify ten regulations for repeal when adding one, subject to exceptions. You’re a San Francisco whistleblower taking five companions to D.C. Your case concerns what gets missed. Washington has announced a quantity discount.
Begin the journey → You leave. The crew keeps every seat belt; counting is not the same as checking what things do.
Scene: San Francisco whistleblower checks an intact seat-belt latch beside a thick blank folder; five companions gather outside the parked van, all safety equipment in its actual state.
Source: Executive order: Unleashing Prosperity Through Deregulation (2025-01-31)
OPEN-WHISTLEBLOWER-C · San Francisco: Pending Review

Trump paused new federal wind approvals for review in 2025. You’re a San Francisco whistleblower taking five companions to D.C. Your case is ready. The folder keeps blowing open, showing a disappointing lack of respect for the memorandum.
Set out for D.C. → You leave San Francisco. A rubber band succeeds where the wind order lacked jurisdiction.

Scene: San Francisco whistleblower catches blank pages lifting from a case folder in an ordinary breeze; five companions and the stationary van wait nearby, with a rubber band lying unused beside the folder.
Source: January 2025 memorandum paused new or renewed federal approvals, permits, leases and loans for wind projects pending review. Th…
